AshNicolus opened PR #103: fix: drop null-keyed rows from a distributed inner join
Closes #96

merge_distributed_inner_join hashed each leg's join column as a raw QueryValue and probed the other leg's raw value against it. QueryValue::Null derives Eq/Ord, so every null-keyed row on one side landed in the same bucket as every null-keyed row on the other, and the join emitted all of them as matches. In Cypher, as in SQL, null = null is not true, so an inner join on a nullable column must drop null-keyed rows on both sides, not treat them as equal.

The in-shard join already gets this right (BindingRow::join refuses to join a null binding against anything). Only this distributed merge treated nulls as a valid join key, so the same query could return different rows depending on whether the planner ran it as one shard-local join or as a cross-cell join.

Skips a null key on both sides of both branches (the right-hashed branch and its left-hashed mirror), on both the build side and the probe side.

Added two tests reproducing the issue's exact repro table, one for each branch (which side ends up hashed depends on which leg has fewer rows). Confirmed both fail with the null check removed and pass with it.

Verified locally: cargo test --lib --features opencypher passes  ...
